correctness.rationale: From characteristic derived ideal [L,L]=kf and bracket relation [e,f]=f, the actual automorphisms are exactly alpha_{u,d}(e)=e+u f, alpha_{u,d}(f)=d f, with u in k and d in k^*. The pairwise-witness condition fixes the e-coordinate and forces Phi(lambda v)=lambda Phi(v) even for zero. This defines the slope function sigma and nonzero kappa; for distinct slopes s,t, a common automorphism requires d=(sigma(t)-sigma(s))/(t-s) !=0, so sigma is injective and hence bijective over the finite field. Conversely any permutation yields such a d on any two distinct nonvertical slopes; a vertical/nonvertical pair forces d=kappa; dependent pairs are handled by homogeneity. Distinct parameters give distinct maps. Genuine automorphisms impose affine sigma(s)=u+ds and kappa=d. The characteristic-two q=2 boundary follows because both slope permutations are affine with d=1. Independent definition-level finite-prime-field enumeration checked all 2, 12 and 480 claimed maps at q=2,3,5 against every ordered pair of input vectors and the full ordinary automorphism group, giving genuine counts 2,6,20. Finite testing is not used to prove all prime powers.

final_claim: Let k=F_q and L=ke+ kf with [e,f]=f. Every 2-local automorphism is uniquely Phi(ae+bf)=ae+a sigma(b/a)f for a!=0 and Phi(bf)=kappa b f for a=0, where sigma is an arbitrary permutation of k and kappa in k^*. Exactly q!(q-1) such maps exist, of which q(q-1) are genuine automorphisms; all 2-local automorphisms are automorphisms iff q=2.
